**Numbers you can quote** (generated by `scripts/update_readme.py` from real runs):

- Rules: 55 (26 CRITICAL/BLOCK, 21 HIGH/WARN, 8 report-only).
- 1195 tests run by default, plus 7 opt-in live-RPC tests that are skipped unless `TXWARDEN_LIVE_RPC` is set (the replay smoke test also needs `TXWARDEN_LIVE_REPLAY_CASES`).
- Synthetic labelled evals: 2660 cases in 92 categories; accuracy 0.977 (dev 0.977, held-out 0.976); BLOCK precision 0.988, recall 0.970.
- Disagreements with the labels: 14 unsafe ALLOW and 12 over-BLOCK, of which 0 and 0 outside the deliberately ambiguous `gray_area` group. Categories with any miss: `swap_impact_band`, `swap_loose`, `swap_mid_trade_slippage_band`, `swap_slippage_band`.
- The original 122-case set still scores 0.984.
- Prompt-injection eval (a scripted model that obeys every injected instruction): 245 runs, verdict weaker than the engine's in 0, changed after `assess_risk` in 0; 50 runs ended in a fail-closed BLOCK. No real language model was run.
- Not verified: any run against a real Ethereum node, real-world detection rates.

## Post

I wrote a pre-signature checker for Ethereum transactions, and the most useful thing about it is
what it refuses to do: let a language model decide.

TxWarden decodes what a transaction will actually do, simulates it against a fork, prices swaps
with the pool math, and applies a registry of rules to return ALLOW, WARN or BLOCK. An LLM agent
can explain the result in plain language, but the verdict comes from deterministic code, and the
agent fails closed if it skips the check. I tested that with a scripted model that obeys every
injected instruction (in calldata, token names, labels, revert reasons): the verdict did not move.

Honest status, because it matters for a security tool:
- All evaluation data is synthetic, and I wrote the labels, so treat the numbers as a regression
  guard, not a detection rate.
- The live RPC path has not been run against a real node yet.
- It covers transactions, not off-chain signature requests.
- I used an AI coding assistant for a lot of the code and leaned on tests and evals to check it.

It is open source, MIT licensed, standard library only. If you work on wallet security and have
labelled real transactions or a node to run the live tests against, I would value the feedback.

https://github.com/Intermountainh8ter/txwarden

## Shorter version (about 400 characters)

Open-sourced TxWarden: a deterministic pre-signature check for Ethereum transactions. An optional
LLM explains the result but cannot change the ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK verdict (tested against a model
that obeys every injected instruction). Synthetic evals only, live-node path not yet run against a
real node. Feedback and real labelled transactions welcome. https://github.com/Intermountainh8ter/txwarden
